ar_sex_boulder_the.blurb: A house-sized block of very hard sandstone sitting beside the trail into the Invasion zone at Cowell. Each side has its own personality: the lower, grayer face holds several powerful bolted lines, the golden streaked face offers thin, technical face climbing, and the uphill side has quieter lines. Boulder problems share the block with the sport routes, and the difficulty runs high, with most of the roped climbs in the 5.12 and 5.13 range. Ab Lounge, Thunderstruck, Electralica and A Fool and His Honey are the ones people come for. Expect a steep, rugged scramble through talus to reach the lower side, and a muddy slot or chimney to get around to the sunny face.
ar_sex_boulder_the.parking_note: Take Cowell Road off Highway 7 for roughly five miles, turn left past the house with the wrecked cars, cross the cattle guard and pull in at the cairn on your right. The campsite sits further up the same track.
ar_sex_boulder_the.approach: Walk the shared trail toward the Invasion Wall, take the sharp left heading downhill, and the block appears on your right as the wall comes into view. The lower side is reached by scrambling talus through a tight corridor.

ar_main_street.blurb: Main Street is one of the busiest sectors at Crystal Bluff, a city-park sandstone crag perched above the Arkansas River in North Little Rock. The routes are almost all bolted sport lines of moderate length, with ledges partway up that make good rests, and the blocky rock gives plenty of crimps and edges. The grades are friendly: the bulk fall between 5.9 and 5.10, with a handful of harder lines above them. Mississippi Queen, Twelve-Bolt Blues, Hydroelectric and Slim Harpo are among the favorites. The belay ledges are small and the wall can be crowded, so bring a leader comfortable placing clips on their own, since there is no way to set up a rope from above.
ar_main_street.parking_note: Follow River Road out of downtown North Little Rock to where it splits at two gates and leave the car on the left. When that gravel patch is full, use the paved lot by the skatepark and boat ramp a short way farther along.
ar_main_street.approach: A short, steep, volunteer-built path climbs from the yellow Crystal Bluff sign at the trailhead up to the base of the wall.

bc_crag_x.blurb: Crag X is a pair of small cliffs, upper and lower, in the Smoke Bluffs, the cluster of crags on the edge of Squamish town. The climbing is mostly traditional crack and corner work on clean granite, with a smaller number of bolted routes. Most of the climbs sit between 5.8 and 5.11, and the 5.10s are what the place is known for: Centre Street, Virgin Soil and Gord's Block are the standouts, along with Fingerlickin' Good and Baby Lizard. Several lines dry quickly after rain, a day or two of sun and wind is often enough, though a few seep for longer. A good choice for building a trad rack's worth of experience close to town.
bc_crag_x.parking_note: In north Squamish turn onto Logger's Lane at the traffic light by the mall, then take the signed right turn a few hundred meters along into the climbers' lot. A gravel road leaves the lot heading south toward the crags.

bc_fern_hill.blurb: Fern Hill is a sport-only cliff up the Mamquam forest road area just north of the Stawamus Chief. The routes are bolted lines on steep to vertical stone, and the grades lean hard: most fall in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, with only a few easier warm-ups. Good Times, Ants Go Marching, Burp the Worm, It's Not About You and Burning the Coil are among the favorites. Some lines are sustained and bouldery, and a few seep for a while after rain, so plan on dry weather. Climbers working through 5.12 will find plenty to keep them busy here.
bc_fern_hill.parking_note: Drive the Powerhouse Springs forest road to its end and use the large lot there, following any visitor-parking signs posted at the time.

bc_c_titanic_north.blurb: Titanic North is a cluster of boulders in the forest below the Stawamus Chief's Grand Wall, near Squamish. It is the more developed half of the Titanic area, with problems from VB through V8 and the bulk of them in the V0 to V4 range, so it suits a wide mix of climbers. Titanic, Snake Hips, Couch Surfer and Titanic Dyno are the easier favorites, while Mantra and Anubis are for stronger climbers. The Grand Wall area is shady and cool, good in summer, and holds slopers and lip traverses. Landings are uneven with rocks and roots, so a couple of smaller pads help. Parking gets tight on summer weekends.
bc_c_titanic_north.approach: The Titanic trail is the southernmost of the trails branching from the Psych Ledge path, starting at the north end of the upper lot. The area is a maze, so a topo helps.

bc_n_easy_chair.blurb: Easy Chair is a bouldering sector in the forest beneath the Chief's Grand Wall, near Squamish. The problems range from V0 to V7, and most sit in the V0 to V6 bracket, with a good spread in the easy and middle grades. Easy in an Easy Chair is the headline climb, with Minor Threat, Lounge Act, Centre Slab, Superdyke and Dyke Surfer close behind. The terrain mixes slabs, seams, dykes and lip traverses on slopers, so the cool, shady air of the Grand Wall forest helps. Landings can be awkward because of rocks and roots, and the trails branch in a maze, so carry a topo and a couple of smaller pads. Summer weekends bring crowded parking.
bc_n_easy_chair.approach: Take the Psych Ledge trail, pass the turn to the BC Parks sign, continue to the outhouse and climb the steps. The Easy Chair boulder is on your right.

bc_little_white.blurb: Little White is a long, quiet wall of short, hard, vertical routes in the White Walls section of Skaha Bluffs, above Skaha Lake near Penticton. It sees far fewer visitors than the busier walls nearby, and the climbing is mostly bolted, with a few trad lines. The grades are stiff: most are 5.11 and 5.12, and almost nothing is easy. Little White itself, Blister in the Sun, Scrotal Cancer and Minor Threat are the highlights. The wall catches the sun in the afternoon, so it suits cooler days or morning starts in summer.
bc_little_white.parking_note: Drive Smythe Drive to where it ends at the pair of lots serving the Bluffs, and use the upper one for the White Walls.
bc_little_white.approach: Take the path just below the upper lot past Daycare and Diamondback. At Elusive Edge bear left to the toilet sign near Go-Anywhere, climb to the crest of the hill, then angle right along a faint path to the wall.

bc_b_morning_glory.blurb: Morning Glory is a busy wall in the northeastern part of Skaha Bluffs, above Skaha Lake near Penticton. It has dozens of moderate to hard routes, nearly all bolted with some trad lines, and a flat bench at the base that makes a comfortable place to hang out. The rock is more featured than much of Skaha, with thin, technical incut holds. Most routes are 5.10 and 5.11, so it works well for intermediates stepping up. Prestadigitor, 'Spro Dog, Being There and Frozen Knuckles are among the favorites. The wall gets morning sun and tips into shade soon after noon, which makes it pleasant in summer.
bc_b_morning_glory.parking_note: Follow Smythe Drive to the end, where two lots serve the Bluffs, and leave the car in the upper one.
bc_b_morning_glory.approach: From just below the upper lot, take the path past Daycare and Diamondback, go right at Elusive Edge toward Grassy Glades, and continue through the cut to The Euphorium. Morning Glory's walls appear on your left soon afterward.

bc_doctors_wall.blurb: Doctors' Wall is among the biggest draws at Skaha Bluffs, above Skaha Lake near Penticton. The wall is tall and steep for the area, with strong, classic lines throughout, almost all bolted. The routes start at 5.10 and are mostly 5.11 and 5.12, with a good number of 5.13s, so it is aimed at experienced sport climbers. The Spell, Naturopath, Doctor MegaTrip, Building a Mystery and Salvation are among the favorites. It has a reputation for staying climbable in damp spells, and shade is easy to find across the group at most hours.
bc_doctors_wall.approach: From the lower lot, follow the main trail past The Fortress and Red Tail to the outhouse crossroads, then follow the sign straight on to Doctors' Group.

bc_bear_mountain_wind_park.blurb: A ridge of weak sandstone and coarse conglomerate cliffs near Dawson Creek, dotted with wind turbines. The bouldering is an adventure rather than a destination: the rock can be soft and not fully solid, and some of it is too poor to climb. Problems run from V0 to V8, with most in the V0 to V4 range. The Steps, closest to the parking, has solid rock, flat landings and plenty of sun. Carlee's Cave holds some of the steepest lines, and the Shaman Cave area has well-liked problems. Wind is common on the ridge, so bring a layer, and plan to carry out any rubbish you find.
bc_bear_mountain_wind_park.parking_note: Reach the ridge via Adams Road and 223 Road, then follow Bear Mountain Road about 2 km to the first turbine, Windmill 34, and leave the car there.
bc_bear_mountain_wind_park.approach: The Steps is a short walk from the parking. The other boulders lie along the scarp and require hiking through the forest.
